samples.summary: Plain-text paste swallows store-write failures, not just clipboard failures
samples.evidence: `pastePlainTextFromClipboard()` (line 4242) puts `this.saveSnapshot()` and the whole `withUndoUnit(() => { deleteSelection(); insertPlainText(text); ... })` inside the same `try` whose `catch {}` is documented as "Clipboard API unavailable or permission denied — silently ignore." Any throw from the write body (docSplitBlock / docInsertText / store batch, e.g. a Yorkie update failure) is therefore discarded with no logging and no user feedback: the batch is rolled back by `Doc.batch` (model refreshed at document.ts:150) and the user simply sees Cmd+Shift+V do nothing, indistinguishable from an empty clipboard. The new test at tests/app/docs/editor-undo-selection.test.ts:432 exercises exactly this path, so the swallow is now on an asserted path. Narrowing the `try` to the `await navigator.clipboard.readText()` would keep write failures visible.

samples.summary: handleInput's `ensureEditableBlock()` write sits outside saveSnapshot() and the undo unit
samples.evidence: In `handleInput`, lines 975-978 call `ensureEditableBlock()` (which does a real store write, `docSplitBlock`, at line 4266) BEFORE `this.saveSnapshot()` (line 1013) and before `withUndoUnit(...)` (line 1019). So typing while the caret sits on a `page-break`/`horizontal-rule` block costs two undo units for one keystroke, and the first Cmd+Z undoes only the split (or, with a selection present, the delete+insert) rather than the whole action — the same one-action/one-unit invariant the delta's tests assert for Enter, page break and plain paste. Reach is one extra unit, not a cap overflow, hence minor; the newly added cases do not cover this shape (their fixture blocks are all paragraphs).

samples.summary: New keydown-driven tests can pass even if the handler throws, because jsdom does not propagate listener exceptions
samples.evidence: `pressKey()` asserts nothing about the dispatch result and jsdom reports an exception thrown inside an event listener to the virtual console rather than rethrowing from `dispatchEvent`. If `handleEnter`/`handlePageBreak` throws after `deleteSelection()`, `Doc.batch` rolls the unit back and refreshes the model (document.ts:146-153), so `getUndoStackForTest().length` can still be `before + 1` (or the undo can still restore `original`) while the action is completely broken — the 'enter over a select-all' case (line 406) has no positive assertion on the resulting document at all, unlike the page-break case which at least checks the inserted block. Consider asserting the post-Enter document shape (e.g. block count grew by one) or failing the test on a captured window error.
